public_rationale: On the stated net-loss reading, the reported 2025 loss of nearly $39 billion exceeds the $14 billion upper-end estimate. This is an underestimate of losses, not evidence that OpenAI performed better than Zitron expected. The verdict is sensitive to the measure: CNBC reported $8 billion of cash burn, and the net-loss report describes substantial restructuring charges. Those figures cannot be substituted silently.
limitations: The speaker did not define loss or specify accounting adjustments.
The verdict changes under a cash-burn ceiling interpretation.
The audited status belongs to the underlying records described by the report; the reported rounded figure is not a directly inspected filing.

our_interpretation: The ordinary financial reading of company losses is its annual bottom-line net loss attributable to the company.
Read 'as much as' as an upper-end estimate of $14 billion, not a prediction of at least $14 billion.
The estimate is based on financial reporting discussed in the context; no GAAP, adjusted-loss, or cash-flow definition is supplied.
Calendar 2025 is the measurement year. Cash burn is a separate measure and cannot substitute for net loss.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable full-year evidence shows a positive net loss no greater than $14 billion under the upper-bound reading.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable full-year evidence shows a net loss greater than $14 billion, or a profit.
